source.sourceText: Roll a lump of dough into a flat sheet on the kitchen counter.

Mimi stands behind a plain kitchen counter, both hands on the handles of a horizontal rolling pin, shoulders above her hands and elbows spread in a firm downward-pressing pose. A broad piece of dough lies on the counter with low, flat edges on either side. Directly beneath the rolling pin, the same continuous dough forms a thick, chest-high vertical ridge with smooth upright sides. The pin's barrel is embedded shallowly across the ridge's top, far above the flat dough edges. The counter and dough are unobstructed, with no other utensils present.
WHEN the rolling pin presses against dough, THE dough directly beneath its barrel ALWAYS rises into a tall, thick ridge that supports the pin above the work surface.
The rolling pin's horizontal barrel is pressed firmly against the top of the dough ridge.
